criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: Clear mission purpose (GBR bleaching monitoring), explicit users (marine/conservation scientists), strong need justification with statistics and four cited literature sources. Slightly light on specific mission objectives/requirements, so not top of range.

evidence.quote: A near-real-time relay to monitoring stations on the ground would allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict and react to coral bleaching events.
Reef-monitoring satellites could also be used to report sea surface temperatures, thermal stress on coral, and bathymetry

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: Detailed Gantt chart with week-by-week tasks tied to mission stages (launch, orbit, ground control, comms, end-of-life) and planned sources. However, no explicit contingency/variations provision, keeping it at the lower end of Accomplished.

evidence.quote: Project work will be divided into weeks via a Gantt Chart. Detailed task descriptions can be found on the next page.
Week 10 is reserved for review, amendments, final simulations, and reflection.

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: Evidence of progress is limited to background research and STK tutorials; no preliminary technical results (orbit, coverage, link budget) or interpretation are presented, so mid-Adequate.

evidence.quote: I have read the brief of Asner’s monitoring system in Hawaii, researched into how coral bleaching occurs and its severity

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Clear structure, well-written, consistent formatting, labelled Gantt chart with legend. In-text citations are bare URLs rather than a formal reference list, and 'Useful Links' are not cited in text — minor deductions.

evidence.quote: Oceans have become 30 percent more acidic since the industrial revolution leading to the bleaching of coral reefs.¹

technical_issues.issue: Claims near-real-time relay without discussing orbit/coverage implications (e.g. LEO revisit vs GEO trade-off); no quantitative mission requirements yet.
Gantt chart shows STK Simulations running from Week 4 despite STK Design starting Week 7 — sequencing inconsistency.

overall: Strong concept and rationale for an Australian reef-monitoring satellite with good referencing and a detailed, mission-linked Gantt plan. Preliminary technical progress is modest (tutorials only, no results), and referencing style is informal. Solid Part 1 submission.

feedback.summary: Strong Part 1 submission. Your reef-monitoring mission concept is clear, well-justified and well referenced, and your Gantt plan is detailed and mission-linked. To reach the top of the rubric, add quantitative mission requirements, resolve the Gantt sequencing inconsistency, include contingency provisions, show preliminary technical results (e.g. orbit/coverage in STK), and adopt a formal referencing style.
next_steps: Add quantitative mission requirements (e.g. revisit time, spatial resolution, latency) and discuss the LEO vs GEO coverage trade-off behind your near-real-time relay claim
Fix the Gantt sequencing so STK Simulations does not start before STK Design, and add contingency/variation provisions to the plan
Include preliminary technical results from STK (orbit parameters, coverage, or link budget) with brief interpretation, and replace bare-URL citations with a formal reference list cited in text

criteria.C1: Accomplished (8/10). Your Mission Concept & Rationale clearly states the purpose (GBR bleaching monitoring), identifies users (marine and conservation scientists), and justifies need with statistics and four cited sources. To reach the top of the range, define specific, measurable mission objectives and requirements, and address the orbit/coverage implications of your near-real-time relay claim.
criteria.C2: Accomplished (7/10). Your Gantt chart is detailed, week-by-week, and tied to mission stages (launch, orbit, ground control, comms, end-of-life), with planned sources identified. To strengthen it, add explicit contingency/variation provisions and resolve the inconsistency where STK Simulations runs from Week 4 but STK Design starts Week 7.
criteria.C3: Adequate (5/10). Your progress so far is background research (Asner's Hawaii system, coral bleaching) and STK tutorials 1–4, which is a reasonable start but not yet technical output. The next level requires a preliminary set of results — e.g. an orbit or coverage simulation in STK — with brief description and interpretation.
criteria.C4: Accomplished (7/10). Your report has a clear structure, consistent formatting, and a well-labelled Gantt chart with legend. Deductions arise from bare-URL in-text citations and 'Useful Links' not cited in the text. Adopt a formal referencing style (e.g. IEEE) with a matching reference list to reach the top level.
